kids.n: ArticleCard — The Kaʿbah, the first House

props.excerpt: The first House set up for people to worship Allah (Qur’ān 3:96). Ibrāhīm and Ismā‘īl raised its foundations, praying: “Our Lord, accept this from us” (2:127).
props.title: The Kaʿbah, the first House

kids.n: ArticleCard — Hājar, Zamzam and the Saʿī

props.excerpt: Alone in the valley with baby Ismā‘īl, Hājar ran seven times between Ṣafā and Marwah until Zamzam burst from the ground. Every pilgrim retraces her steps.
props.title: Hājar, Zamzam and the Saʿī

props.excerpt: The Prophet migrated from Makkah to Yathrib, which became Madinah. The Islamic calendar counts its years from this journey.
props.title: The Hijrah to Madinah

kids.n: ArticleCard — The change of the Qiblah

props.excerpt: Sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah, the direction of prayer turned from Jerusalem to the Ka‘bah (Qur’ān 2:144).
props.title: The change of the Qiblah

props.excerpt: About 700 Muslims faced 3,000 fighters of Quraysh below the mountain the Prophet loved. Allah speaks of it in Sūrah Āl ‘Imrān.
props.title: The Battle of Uhud

props.excerpt: The only Ḥajj the Prophet made after the Hijrah. His rites and his sermon at ‘Arafah became the model every pilgrim follows.
props.title: The Farewell Pilgrimage

kids.n: Mount Uḥud rises about 5 km north of the Prophet’s Mosque. In Shawwāl 3 AH, an army of Quraysh marched on Madinah to avenge their defeat at Badr, and the two sides met on the plain below the mountain.

kids.n: FaqItem — Can I put on Ihrām at home or on the plane?

props.answer: Yes, you can wear the Iḥrām clothes before you travel. What matters is the intention: make it, with the Talbiyah, at the mīqāt or before it. On a plane, make it when the crew announces you are passing the mīqāt. Crossing the mīqāt without Iḥrām means going back to it; if you can’t, most scholars say a sacrifice (dam) is due.
props.question: Can I put on Ihrām at home or on the plane?

kids.n: FaqItem — Can I use scented soap or deodorant?

props.answer: Not once you are in Iḥrām — switch to unscented products. Perfume on your body before entering Iḥrām is Sunnah, even if the scent lingers afterwards.
props.question: Can I use scented soap or deodorant?

kids.n: FaqItem — I broke an Ihrām rule by mistake. What now?

props.answer: Stop as soon as you realise — take off the item or wash off the scent. Many scholars say there is no penalty if you forgot or didn’t know; others require a fidyah. If it happens, ask a scholar about your case.
props.question: I broke an Ihrām rule by mistake. What now?

kids.n: FaqItem — I lost count of my rounds. What do I do?

props.answer: Go with the number you are sure of — the lower one — and carry on from there. Doubts that come after you have finished don’t count.
props.question: What if I lose count of my Ṭawāf circuits?

kids.n: FaqItem — Do I need wudūʾ for Saʿī?

props.answer: Most scholars say wuḍū’ is required for Ṭawāf but only recommended for Sa‘ī. If you lose it during Sa‘ī, you can carry on.
props.question: Do I need wudūʾ for Saʿī?

kids.n: FaqItem — Can I stop to rest, drink or pray?

props.answer: Yes. A short rest or a drink of water is fine. If the congregational prayer starts, join it, then continue from where you stopped.
props.question: Can I stop to rest, drink or pray?

kids.n: FaqItem — Can I do Ṭawāf and Saʿī in a wheelchair?

props.answer: Yes. Someone can push you, and wheelchairs are available at the Ḥaram. The Prophet told Umm Salamah, who was unwell, to do Ṭawāf riding behind the people.
props.question: Can I do Ṭawāf and Saʿī in a wheelchair?

kids.n: FaqItem — My period started. Can I still do ʿUmrah?

props.answer: Yes. Enter Iḥrām at the mīqāt as normal and do everything except Ṭawāf. Wait until you are pure, take a bath (ghusl), then do Ṭawāf and Sa‘ī.
props.question: My period started. Can I still do ʿUmrah?

kids.n: FaqItem — Do I need a mahram to travel for ʿUmrah?

props.answer: Scholars differ. Many hold that a woman needs a maḥram to travel; others allow travel in a safe, trusted group. Saudi Arabia currently lets women perform ‘Umrah without one. Follow the view of scholars you trust.
props.question: Do I need a mahram to travel for ʿUmrah?

kids.n: FaqItem — Can I do more than one ʿUmrah on this trip?

props.answer: Scholars differ. Those who allow it say to leave the Ḥaram boundary and enter Iḥrām again, for example at Masjid ‘Ā’ishah in at-Tan‘īm. Others say extra Ṭawāf is better, since the Prophet didn’t repeat ‘Umrah on one trip.
props.question: Can I do more than one ʿUmrah on this trip?

kids.n: FaqItem — Is there a farewell Ṭawāf after ʿUmrah?

props.answer: Most scholars say the farewell Ṭawāf is only obligatory for Ḥajj. After ‘Umrah it is recommended, not required.
props.question: Is there a farewell Ṭawāf after ʿUmrah?

props.text: Where scholars differ, these answers follow the majority view. For your own situation, ask a scholar you trust.
